run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend since 2026-11-16T15:26:28Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate alert is firing because the frontend returned HTTP 500 on its /api/data (and, less often, /api/checkout) routes after its dependencies became unreachable. At 2026-11-16T15:24:54Z the Deployments ad and payment in namespace otel-demo were rollout-restarted (new ReplicaSets ad-6cb57f76d and payment-9c8ffb665 whose pod template carries kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-16T15:24:54Z, image unchanged). The replacement pods were marked Ready within seconds although the pod templates define no readiness/startup probe, so the Services sent traffic to containers that were still starting while pinned at very small CPU limits (ad 50m, payment 20m) with 90-100% CFS throttling. frontend's gRPC calls to the ad Service ClusterIP 100.65.180.246:8080 failed with '14 UNAVAILABLE ... connect ECONNREFUSED', and checkout's calls to the payment ClusterIP 100.70.188.60:8080 failed the same way. frontend's own error-status span rate went from exactly 0 to 3.03 spans/s in the 15:25-15:26 minute, peaked at 13.6 spans/s at 15:27:00, and returned to 0 by 15:34, matching the alert start at 15:26:28Z. ad stopped serving GetAds entirely from 15:27 to 15:34 and resumed ~15:34; payment's Charge span rate was 0 in the 15:26-15:27 and 15:27-15:28 minutes and resumed by 15:31. The dominant error source is the ad dependency; a smaller subset is payment. No node, cluster-wide, or other service failure was observed, and the pods were replaced by their own controllers (not crashed, not OOMKilled, not Evicted).

claims.text: frontend emitted zero STATUS_CODE_ERROR spans in every 5-minute window from 15:03:28 through 15:25:28; the error-span rate first became non-zero at the 15:26:28 evaluation (0.337 spans/s) and was back to 0 from 15:37:28 onward, matching the alert's 15:26:28Z start.

At 1-minute resolution, frontend error spans first appear in the 15:25:00-15:26:00 minute (3.03 spans/s), peak at 13.6 spans/s at 15:27:00, stay elevated through the 15:33 minute (5.6 spans/s) and are 0 in the 15:34 and 15:35 minutes.

frontend's error spans are concentrated in one call path: increase() over 14:26:28-15:42:32 returned 387.1 error spans for operation 'GET /api/data', 387.1 for frontend's client span 'GET', 387.1 for 'grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds', 42.7 for 'POST /api/checkout', 42.7 for 'executing api route (pages) /api/checkout', 42.7 for 'grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder' and 15.2 for 'tcp.connect'; all other frontend operations had zero error spans.

Failing /api/data traces (e.g. trace_id f5de8913626ea0f07fc497d12453936c, 15:26:01Z) show frontend 'GET /api/data' with http.status_code=500 / otel.status_code=ERROR, and its child span 'grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds' with rpc.grpc.status_code=14 and grpc.error_message '14 UNAVAILABLE: No connection established. Last error: connect ECONNREFUSED 100.65.180.246:8080'.

The otel-demo Service 'ad' is a ClusterIP service with clusterIP 100.65.180.246, port 8080 -> targetPort 8080 and selector opentelemetry.io/name=ad; that is exactly the address refused in the frontend error. The Service 'payment' similarly has clusterIP 100.70.188.60, port 8080.

Failing checkout traces (e.g. trace_id d6cdbb77a6efa02b856135c6df0b25e4, 15:26:01Z) show checkout's span 'oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge' with rpc.grpc.status_code=14 and message 'connection error: ... dial tcp 100.70.188.60:8080: connect: connection refused', and the parent 'oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder' returning rpc.grpc.status_code=13 'failed to charge card', surfacing as frontend HTTP 500 on 'POST /api/checkout'.

At 15:24:54Z the ad Deployment scaled up new ReplicaSet ad-6cb57f76d (0->1) and scaled ad-554b849958 from 1 to 0; ad-554b849958-mbnxm was stopped/deleted and ad-6cb57f76d-xmcq6 was created, scheduled to node i-0e9f8b08cc290a884 and its container started at 15:24:56. The identical sequence occurred for payment (new ReplicaSet payment-9c8ffb665, old payment-55766d76b9 deleted, new pod payment-9c8ffb665-qrm84 on the same node).

Both new ReplicaSet pod templates are annotated kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-16T15:24:54Z (deployment revision 2 vs revision 1 before), keep the same images (ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-ad, ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-payment), and specify no readinessProbe, livenessProbe or startupProbe; CPU limits are 50m (ad) and 20m (payment).

The replacement pods were reported Ready almost immediately (ad-6cb57f76d-xmcq6 Ready at 15:24:57Z, payment-9c8ffb665-qrm84 Ready at 15:24:58Z) with restartCount 0 and no previous terminated container, and the ad Service's endpoint is now backed by ad-6cb57f76d-xmcq6 (100.96.4.142:8080).

ad served GetAds until the 15:25-15:26 minute (1.23 spans/s), then its GetAds server-span rate was exactly 0 for the 15:27, 15:28, 15:31, 15:32, 15:33 and 15:34 minutes and resumed at 2.4 spans/s in the 15:34-15:35 minute.

payment's own 'charge' server-span rate fell from 1.4 spans/s to 0.767 spans/s in the 15:25-15:26 minute, was 0 in the 15:26-15:27 and 15:27-15:28 minutes, and was back at 1.0-1.4 spans/s from the 15:30-15:31 minute onward; payment recorded zero STATUS_CODE_ERROR spans throughout.

During the outage the replacement ad container was CPU-throttled in 0.90-1.00 of CFS periods (5-minute throttle ratio at 15:26-15:32) with CPU usage reaching ~0.049 cores, i.e. its 50m limit, and the replacement payment container was throttled in 0.998 of periods at 15:26 falling to ~0.38 by 15:32 with usage up to ~0.0148 cores against its 20m limit.

Retained container logs show request handling resuming at 15:33:14Z (payment: 'Charge request received.') and 15:33:50Z (ad: 'Targeted ad request received for [...]'), with the ad stream ending 15:34:20Z and the payment stream ending 15:34:23Z.

Server-side error evidence besides frontend: checkout had a non-zero error-span rate from 15:27 to 15:31 (0.32 spans/s at 15:27:00 falling to 0.244 spans/s at 15:31:00, 0.0148 at 15:32:00, 0 from 15:33:00), while ad, payment, cart, product-catalog, currency, accounting, shipping, email, quote and recommendation recorded 0 error spans (fraud-detection and recommendation only ~0.0037 spans/s sporadic pre-existing noise). frontend-proxy error rate mirrored frontend (0.17 spans/s at 15:26:00 rising to 2.39 spans/s at 15:31:00).

In the same failed traces, frontend-proxy spans ('ingress', 'router frontend egress') and load-generator spans ('GET'/'POST') carry http.status_code=500 / error=true, i.e. the 500s propagated out to the proxy and the synthetic client.

The ad and payment pods were replaced by their own Deployments' controllers, not damaged: events show SuccessfulCreate/SuccessfulDelete and ScalingReplicaSet for both Deployments, the new containers have restartCount 0 and no previous terminated container, and no OOMKilled or Evicted event was returned.
A node-level cause is not supported: all five nodes report Ready=True with no MemoryPressure, DiskPressure or PIDPressure, including node i-0e9f8b08cc290a884 which hosts both replacement pods.

A broad platform fault or other service failure is not supported: frontend's error rate was exactly 0 before 15:25, the only pods created at 15:24:54-58 were the ad and payment replacements (every other otel-demo pod started around 14:51), and cart, product-catalog, currency, accounting, shipping, email, quote and recommendation recorded zero error spans through the window.

An ad application-level failure such as flagd flag-evaluation errors is not the cause of the frontend errors: ad's only error spans are 'flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream' spans with rpc.grpc.status_code=4 / 'stream closed due to server-side timeout' seen at 14:56-15:16 (before the incident) plus a tiny ~0.0037 spans/s residue, whereas the frontend failure is the exact text 'connect ECONNREFUSED 100.65.180.246:8080', i.e. no TCP connection to the ad Service was established at all.

Root mechanism: the 15:24:54Z rollout restart of the single-replica ad (and payment) Deployments replaced a serving pod with one that Kubernetes marked Ready and placed in Service endpoints immediately (no readiness/startup probe), while the new container was pinned at its 50m CPU limit and throttled in ~90-100% of CFS periods during startup; the app therefore was not listening on 8080 for several minutes, so the Service ClusterIP returned connection refused until ad resumed serving around 15:34 and payment around 15:30-15:31.

The checkout failures are a second, separate consequence of the same rollout action and are attributable to the payment restart rather than to ad: the checkout error text names the payment ClusterIP 100.70.188.60:8080, payment's Charge span rate dropped to 0 in the 15:26-15:28 minutes, and it accounts for the smaller part of the alert (42.7 of the ~1,307 error spans reported by increase() vs 387.1 for the ad path).

Add a readiness probe (or startup probe) to the ad and payment containers and provision enough CPU for startup, so a restarted pod is not added to Service endpoints before it is listening on 8080; also avoid restarting the single-replica ad and payment Deployments simultaneously without such probes.

gaps: The RequestErrorRate alerting rule could not be read: list_prometheus_rules returned no rule for rule_name=RequestErrorRate and no alerting rules at all, so the rule expression and the annotation's current value 2.5777777777777775 could not be reproduced or verified; the frontend error-rate series I measured is the only independently observed error signal.

Startup-phase container logs are unavailable: fetches restricted to 15:24:00-15:26:00 for the new ad pod and the new payment pod returned no lines, and the retained streams begin after 15:26 and end at 15:34:20/15:34:23, so why the applications needed minutes to listen is inferred from CPU-throttling metrics, not from startup log lines.
frontend container logs returned 0 lines in the window, so frontend's own application-level error logging could not be corroborated; its error evidence comes from spans and metrics only.

payment's own failure evidence is indirect: it emitted no error spans and kept some Charge traffic, so the exact duration and share of refused connections to 100.70.188.60:8080 during 15:26-15:31 is unknown.
Jaeger's stored traces end at about 15:26:03Z for this window, so trace-level detail after 15:26 is unavailable and the later part of the incident is attested only by metrics and logs.
The change_history integration is not available in this Run, so who or what issued the 15:24:54Z rollout restart (the kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt annotation) is unknown.

The duration of the initial (14:51) start of these pods is unknown because metric data begins at 15:03, so I cannot say whether the observed multi-minute startup is specific to this restart or normal for these CPU limits.
next_steps: Confirm with the change owner whether a kubectl rollout restart of the ad and payment Deployments was intentionally issued at 2026-11-16T15:24:54Z.
Add readiness/startup probes and review CPU limits for ad and payment to prevent endpoints receiving traffic before the process binds port 8080.
Retrieve the RequestErrorRate alerting rule definition (expression, threshold, for-duration) from the Alertmanager/Prometheus configuration store, since it is not loaded in the queried Prometheus.
